messages.text: 11c. but I dont see how it beats buy and hold btc. for a price of 899, and typical lifetime of these machines, also considering the limited warranty, it would take for how many years exactly to break even? and the halving will happen before that. too many years.

At home power the sats usually come to less than the electricity — that's not why people buy it. So no, it won't beat stacking $899 of BTC on a spreadsheet.

What you're buying at 11¢ (~$32 a month) is a draw at a full 3.125 BTC block every ten minutes, for years, and you keep the machine after every draw. Plus you actually run a node-and-pool setup instead of reading about it.

If that shot isn't interesting to you, buy-and-hold is the cleaner call — I'd rather say that than sell you one. Is the lottery angle any part of why you were looking?

lottery angle is not what I'm looking for, feels more like a gamble, rather then reliable investment. the rates of winning a lottery with something like this is 1/600~ every year or so? I don't have 600 more years to live, and the machine wont make it past 5 years, average. what are you selling then?

Then I'm selling you the other two things, and if neither lands, I'd tell you to keep your $899.

Steady sats: pointed at a pool it pays out small and regular, straight to your own wallet, no exchange, no KYC. Less than the power bill at 11¢, as I said — but it's Bitcoin you mined, not bought.

And the learning: a real machine on your desk teaching you pools, wallets, difficulty and firmware. Most first buyers are really buying that.

If you want a reliable investment, this isn't one, and I won't dress it up. Which of those two, if either, is worth $899 to you?

both are sweet, but not sure if worth the price. Seems more like a hobbyist kind of investment, fun toy, per say, rather then investment hoping for ROI, right? how long would you estimate this would take to pay for itself, assuming it doesnt break before, and btc is priced at 100k, but halving is in 2 years?

Yes — hobbyist is the honest word for it, and I'm not going to argue you out of it.

On payback: at home power the sats usually come to less than the electricity — that's not why people buy it. So I can't hand you a break-even date, and the halving in two years cuts the sats side again. Any number I gave you would be made up.

What people do buy it for is the machine itself: real mining on your own gear, your own wallet, something you keep and learn on. At $899 that's a toy with teeth, not a return.

If the ROI question is the one that matters to you, the answer is buy the BTC instead. Want me to leave it there, or is there a cheaper way in you'd rather look at?

well here's another angle. the machine is not out yet, noone unbiased had properly evaluated it and shared the results. only some influences which prob got it for free to review, and mainly the developer/owner/creator. feels like hard to trust, while also having to wait for this payment of 899 to be compensated only in 2~ more months, since it's not instant delivery
Read the hammer miner thor p2 page
Read the hammer miner bc04 page

That's the fairest objection you've raised, and I won't talk it down. The B30 is a pre-sale — Batch 5 ships November 30, 2026 — and B30 dates have moved before. Independent reviews of a unit nobody has yet don't exist.

Two things that actually help: an unshipped pre-order is refundable in full, no restocking fee, so your $899 isn't locked for two months. And you don't have to start at $899.

The Hammer BC04 is $239, 6 TH/s, ~100 W — about $8 a month at your 11¢ — in stock and shipping in a few days. Real miner, real pool payouts, your wallet, cheap tuition. If you like it, the B30 will still be there with reviews attached by then.

Want me to build that one?

bc04 doesn't have the efficiency B30 advertises. I'm only looking at this because it's actually somewhat meaningfully cheaper to run then btc it mines. TH/j (or j/TH) is much better, almost single digits

You're right on both counts. BC04 is 100 W for 6 TH — about 16.7 J/TH. The B30's page figures are 405 W at the wall for 30 TH, so ~13.5 J/TH. Better, but not single digits, and that's the manufacturer's number on a unit nobody independent has metered yet.

So if efficiency is the whole reason you're here, the B30 is the best we list — and the honest caveat is that 13.5 stays a spec until units land in buyers' hands on November 30.

At 11¢ that's about $32 a month to run it. Nothing in our lineup beats it on J/TH today.

Do you want it, or would you rather wait for the first real teardowns before you commit $899?

assuming btc goes up in the upcoming months, drastically, once the pre-orders ship, do these units tend to cost more later? not to create myself a FOMO (not much to miss out on, expensive hobbyist toy), but curious if prices tend to spike.

Honestly: our own prices have only gone one way so far. The B30 launched at $799, went to $849, then $899 on September 15. The Magic Miner went $649, $749, now $799 by batch. Earlier buyers keep what they paid.

But that was cost and redesign, not the BTC price — the B30's cooling was reengineered around the BM1373 and that pushed the cost up. I can't tell you what a rally would do; nobody here can.

Across the industry hardware does firm up in a bull run, but I'm not going to turn that into a reason to buy tonight. If you're not sold on the hobby, a $100 price move shouldn't decide it.

context.pop: At 10¢ the Harlo B30 runs about $29 a month, at 16¢ about $47 — what do you pay for power?
